subject: green sea turtle
title: Almost Every Turtle on This Reef Is Female, and the Sand Decides

scenes.text: Almost every turtle on this reef is female.
On the northern Great Barrier Reef, about 99 percent of young green turtles are girls.
scenes.keywords: green sea turtle great barrier reef

scenes.text: It isn't food. It isn't genes. A turtle's sex depends on how warm its nest is.
scenes.keywords: green sea turtle nest sand eggs

scenes.text: Warmer sand makes females. The hottest northern nests hatch almost all female.
Cooler beaches to the south are only about two thirds female.
The sand picks the sex. The turtle never gets a say.

description:
Almost every turtle on this reef is female.
On the northern Great Barrier Reef, about 99 percent of young green turtles are female, because warm nest sand produces females. Cooler beaches to the south are around 65 to 69 percent female.
Did you know temperature could decide an animal's sex?
first_comment: Temperature decides the sex of many reptiles. Did you expect that from a turtle nest?
